t: In which year were reinsurance pools in the Fire and Hull classes first initiated in India by the Indian Insurance Companies Association?
e: The Fire and Hull reinsurance pools were initiated in 1966 by the Indian Insurance Companies Association, well before GIC was formed in 1972.

t: GIC was constituted under which enactment?
e: GIC was formed in 1972 under GIBNA, the General Insurance Business (Nationalisation) Act, 1972.

t: GIC was notified as the Indian reinsurer in which month and year?
e: The IRDA Act, 1999 came into force in April 2000 and GIC was notified as the Indian reinsurer in November 2000.

t: What does SWIFT at GIC Re stand for?
o: Single Window International Facultative and Treaty
Statutory Window for Indian Facultative Transactions
Society for Worldwide Insurance Facultative Transfers
Standard Working Interface for Facultative Treaties
e: SWIFT is GIC Re's Single Window International Facultative and Treaty facility for non-reciprocal inward business.

t: A.M. Best's National Scale Rating of GIC Re, as cited in the material, is
e: A.M. Best rates GIC Re with FSR A- (Excellent), long-term ICR A- (Excellent) and a National Scale Rating of aaa (Exceptional); CARE gives it AAA Stable.

t: Which pool has a corpus of Rs 500 crore and GIC Re as its designated manager?
o: Indian Market Terrorism Risk Insurance Pool
e: GIC Re is designated manager of INIP and the Fertilizer pool, the latter having a corpus of Rs 500 crore.

t: For business placed with the terrorism and nuclear pools, the obligatory cession to GIC Re
o: applies at 5% on the pool share
applies at 4% before the pool share
applies only on the retained portion
does not apply, as 100% goes to the pool
e: For terrorism and nuclear risks 100% of the business goes to the respective pool and no obligatory cession is applicable.

t: A single non-marine fire loss of ₹100 crore is suffered by OICL. Under its Risk XL of ₹575 crore xs ₹25 crore, the recovery is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The reinsurer pays the loss above the ₹25 crore deductible: 100 − 25 = ₹75 crore, within the ₹575 crore limit.

t: As a thumb rule, retention on a property risk should not exceed what proportion of the insurer's net worth?
e: The thumb rule is property risk retention up to 5% of net worth and non-property risk retention up to 1-2% of net worth, with no hard and fast rule.

t: An insurer has a net worth of ₹2,000 crore. Applying the thumb rule in the material, the indicative maximum retention on a single property risk is
e: Property retention is up to 5% of net worth: 5% of ₹2,000 crore = ₹100 crore.

t: Under the hours clause of a catastrophe treaty, the time limit for aggregating losses from a cyclone is typically
e: The hours clause limits a loss occurrence to losses within a stated period, usually 72 consecutive hours for cyclone/windstorm.

t: A power plant with sum insured ₹200 crore exceeds the fire treaty capacity. The correct course for the underwriting officer is to
o: seek facultative support for the portion above the treaty capacity
retain the excess on the company's net account
cede the entire risk to the fac-oblig treaty
decline the risk outright as it is beyond treaty
e: Facultative reinsurance is used for risks exceeding treaty limits; the insurer places the portion above treaty capacity facultatively.

t: In the event of war between India and the reinsurer's country, the treaty
e: The commencement and termination clause provides for automatic termination in case of war between India and the reinsurer's country.

t: Under the accounting clause, the reinsurer must confirm the accounts rendered by the ceding insurer within
o: 7 days of receipt, and balances are paid within 15 days
90 days of receipt, and balances are paid at the year end
30 days of receipt, and balances are paid within 30 days
15 days of receipt, and balances are paid within 15 days of confirmation
e: The accounting clause requires confirmation within 15 days of receipt and settlement of balances on either side within 15 days of such confirmation.

t: Under a facultative obligatory treaty
o: both parties are free to cede or accept
the insurer may cede and the reinsurer must accept
both parties must cede and accept
the insurer must cede and the reinsurer may accept
e: Fac-oblig is a hybrid in which the ceding insurer has the option to cede but the reinsurer is bound to accept whatever is ceded.

t: Which of the following is an Indian credit rating agency?
e: Indian agencies listed are CARE, CRISIL, ICRA, ONICRA and SMERA; S&P, Moody's, Fitch, Duff & Phelps and A.M. Best are global agencies.

t: In a surplus treaty, the ceding insurer's retention out of the sum insured is called a
e: One line equals the cedant's retention, and the treaty capacity is expressed as a number of lines.

t: Retention is ₹5 lakh and a risk has sum insured ₹30 lakh. How many lines are ceded to the surplus treaty?
e: Surplus = 30 − 5 = ₹25 lakh; 25 ÷ 5 = 5 lines ceded.

t: When the surplus cession is decided on a PML basis rather than sum insured, the effect on the ceding insurer is that
e: On PML basis the cedant retains a larger share of the risk and hence more premium, and its need for surplus protection reduces; PML is not a limit of liability.

t: A reinsurer provides a Cat XL limit of ₹100 crore for a premium of ₹5 crore. The rate on line is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Rate on line = premium ÷ limit of cover = 5 ÷ 100 = 5%; it reduces for each successive higher layer.

t: Under a 40% quota share treaty a claim of ₹10 lakh is settled. The reinsurer's share is
e: Quota share applies the fixed percentage to sum insured, premium and claims alike: 40% of ₹10 lakh = ₹4 lakh.

t: The burning cost method of rating is considered suitable for
e: Burning cost (historical rating on the last five years' experience) suits working XL; catastrophe covers are unsuitable for it since loss experience may be unavailable.

t: In the variable quota share example, retention is 7.5% on a sum insured of ₹50,00,000. The ceding insurer's share is
e: 7.5% of ₹50 lakh = ₹3,75,000 retained; the reinsurer takes ₹46,25,000.

t: Quota share is considered more profitable to a reinsurer than surplus because
o: the cedant bears all small claims
the reinsurer receives no ceding commission
both parties participate in every risk on the same basis
e: Since the reinsurer shares every risk on the same basis, there is no selection against the reinsurer, which is why quota share treaties also earn higher ceding commission.

t: With a retention of ₹5 lakh and a 1st surplus of 5 lines, a risk of sum insured ₹75 lakh leaves how much for the 2nd surplus?
e: Retention ₹5 lakh + 1st surplus ₹25 lakh = ₹30 lakh; the balance ₹45 lakh (9 lines) goes to the 2nd surplus.

t: In the reinsurance arrangement table, a risk of ₹200 crore (4% statutory cession, ₹5 crore net retention, 20% quota share, 1st surplus max ₹40 crore, 2nd surplus max ₹35 crore) requires facultative placement of
e: 8 + 5 + 40 + 40 + 35 = ₹128 crore is absorbed by the programme; 200 − 128 = ₹72 crore must be placed facultatively.

t: An insurer cedes ₹500 crore of reinsurance premium outside India. The maximum it may place with a single CBR rated 'A' (S&P) is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). A rating above BBB+ and up to A+ carries a 15% limit: 15% of ₹500 crore = ₹75 crore.

t: A treaty written on a 'worldwide' territorial basis is understood to
e: By market convention 'worldwide' in a treaty means worldwide excluding USA and Canada.

t: A bordereau submitted to the reinsurer under a proportional treaty is
o: a summary of the cedant's balance sheet
a list of risks ceded with insured name, class, SI, rate, retention, amount reinsured and period
a notice of cancellation of the treaty
a statement of the reinsurer's security rating
e: The bordereau details each risk ceded and is submitted monthly or quarterly as agreed.

t: In computing the reinsurance premium under a proportional treaty, commission paid by the ceding insurer to agents and brokers is
o: not deducted from the reinsurance premium
e: The reinsurer receives the same percentage of the original gross premium as of the sum insured; agency commission is not deducted (except where original net rate applies).

t: The level of ceding commission under a 2nd surplus treaty is normally
o: lower than under the 1st surplus treaty
higher than under the 1st surplus treaty
equal to the quota share commission
e: Commission is highest for quota share, lower for surplus, and still lower for the higher surplus treaties like the 2nd and 3rd.

t: Profit of a treaty for the purpose of profit commission equals
o: earned premium − incurred claims − ceding commission
earned premium − incurred claims + ceding commission
e: Profit commission is a percentage of treaty profit, computed as earned premium less incurred claims less ceding commission.

t: Under an original net rate arrangement, used for classes like marine, the premium paid to the reinsurer is
o: the original premium less the original commission
e: ORC means premium is ceded net of original commission, and only a small percentage of commission (ORC) is then allowed by the reinsurer.

t: The IRDAI portal through which a policyholder can escalate an unresolved grievance against an insurer is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Bima Bharosa (formerly IGMS) is the grievance portal; Bima Sugam is the marketplace, Bima Vahak the women-led distribution channel and Bima Vistaar the combined rural product.

t: Salvage recovered on a loss ceded under a surplus treaty must be
o: shared with the reinsurer in the same proportion as the sum insured
retained wholly by the ceding insurer
e: Recoveries by salvage, contribution and subrogation are shared in the same proportion as the sum insured, just as claims and claim costs are.

t: The additional premium paid by a ceding insurer so that a new treaty covers policies already in force at inception is called
e: A portfolio entry premium brings in-force policies into a new treaty; a portfolio withdrawal premium is paid by the reinsurer to cut off cover at termination.

t: The facility of portfolio entry and withdrawal premium does not apply to
e: Marine and aviation treaties are written on an underwriting year basis, with premium and losses accounted retrospectively to the treaty year, so portfolio transfers are not used.

t: Where a quota share treaty is followed by a surplus treaty, the entire quota share treaty treated as the line is termed the
e: The whole quota share treaty is taken as the gross line; the cedant's own retention under the quota share is the net line.

t: The document that sets out the risk particulars and the terms for which reinsurance protection is sought is the
e: The slip lists reassured, period, business, exclusions, territory, retention, commission, profit commission and reinsurer.

t: Which of the following is NOT another name for retention under an excess of loss cover?
e: In XL cover the retention is called deductible, excess, priority or underlying; 'line' is a surplus treaty term.

t: A per-risk XL treaty has a priority of ₹50 lakh and a limit of ₹2 crore. A single loss of ₹1.5 crore occurs. The reinsurer pays
e: The reinsurer pays the loss above the priority up to the limit: 1.5 − 0.5 = ₹1 crore.

t: A storm damages five factories. The per-risk XL treaty is ₹25 lakh xs ₹25 lakh with an event limit of three times the per-risk limit. Claims paid are ₹50L, ₹47.5L, ₹30L, ₹42.5L and ₹35L. The total reinsurance recovery is
e: Per-risk recoveries are 25 + 22.5 + 5 + 17.5 + 10 = ₹80 lakh, but the event limit of 3 × 25 = ₹75 lakh caps the recovery.

t: The Risk XL (non-marine) protection of OICL cited in the material is
e: OICL's Risk XL (non-marine) is ₹575 crore excess of ₹25 crore; the Cat XL covers are ₹1,200 crore xs ₹50 crore (all perils) and ₹2,900 crore xs ₹50 crore (EQ).

t: A stop loss treaty pays 90% of the loss ratio in excess of 80% subject to a maximum loss ratio of 130%. In a year with loss ratio 85%, the reinsurer pays
e: Excess over 80% is 5%; the reinsurer pays 90% of it = 4.5%, leaving the cedant with 80% + 0.5%.

t: Under a stop loss cover with retention 85% and limit up to 120%, the actual loss ratio is 110%. The reinsurer bears
e: The reinsurer pays the loss ratio above 85% up to 120%: 110 − 85 = 25%.

t: Retention per event is ₹10 crore and the probable maximum number of risks involved in one event (PMN) is 20. The retention per risk works out to
e: Retention per risk = retention per event ÷ PMN = 10 crore ÷ 20 = ₹50 lakh.

t: An insurer must resolve a policyholder's grievance within how many days of receipt?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). 14 days under the 2024 regulations; thereafter the policyholder may approach Bima Bharosa or the Ombudsman.

t: Premiums ceded during the year are ₹1,00,000, incoming premium reserve ₹55,000 and outgoing premium reserve ₹20,000. The earned premium is
e: Earned premium = premium ceded + unexpired premium reserve at the beginning − unexpired premium reserve at the end = 1,00,000 + 55,000 − 20,000.

t: A general insurer's Board-approved reinsurance programme with retention policy for the coming financial year must be filed with IRDAI
o: 45 days before the commencement of the financial year
30 days before the commencement of the financial year
within 30 days of the commencement of the financial year
e: The draft programme is due 45 days before the FY starts; the final programme or CEO declaration within 30 days of commencement; revisions within 15 days of Board approval.

t: The maximum overall cession allowed to a cross border reinsurer rated greater than A+ (S&P or equivalent) is
o: 10% of the total reinsurance premium ceded outside India
20% of the total reinsurance premium ceded outside India
15% of the total reinsurance premium ceded outside India
50% of the total reinsurance premium ceded outside India
e: Cession limits per CBR are 20% for above A+, 15% for above BBB+ up to A+, and 10% for BBB and BBB+, computed on total premium ceded outside India.
